y1: “Be careful that you don't do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them.” Jesus says that hypocrites blow trumpets when they give charity.
y2: “They have received their reward in full.” That means people's praise is all the reward they will get.
y3: Charity, prayer, and fasting were the three pillars of Jewish piety. Jesus did not abolish them. At the end of all three comes the same refrain: “Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
y5: In those days, houses had a small storage room for grain and tools, without even a window. Jesus says to go in there, close the door, and pray.
y6: Do not think you will be heard for your many words like the pagans. Because God is a 'Father' who already knows.
y7: In the Sermon on the Mount, the word 'Father' appears 17 times, 10 of which are in 6:1–18. Prayer is not transmitting information, but a relationship with the Father.
y9: “Pray like this.” The first three requests of the Lord's Prayer ask for the 'Father's' name, Kingdom, and will, while the last three ask for 'our' bread, debts, and temptation.
y10: God's work comes first, my needs come second. But my needs are not forgotten. The Father cares about both.
y11: The word 'I' does not appear even once in the Lord's Prayer. 'Our Father', 'our bread', 'our debts'. Even if we pray alone in our room, we pray together with God's whole family.
y13: Jesus explains only one request from the Lord's Prayer again: forgiveness. “If you don't forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.”
y14: When you fast, do not look gloomy, but anoint your head and wash your face. Faith is not a performance.
y15: This does not mean 'buying' forgiveness. A forgiven person becomes a forgiving person. If we reject forgiving to the end, we need to examine whether we have truly accepted God's forgiveness (18:21–35).
verse: “But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
prayer: Our Father in heaven, help me to be free from a faith meant to be seen, and to live sincerely before You. May I seek Your name, Your Kingdom, and Your will before my own needs. As a forgiven person, let me also forgive. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: hypocrite. It originally referred to an actor playing a role with a mask. It is a faith where the inside and outside are different. The English word 'hypocrite' comes from this.
d1: charity. It comes from the word 'mercy'. Helping is imitating God's mercy. The Azerbaijani word 'sədəqə' is also used in everyday life.
d2: room. It was a small room inside the house where grain and valuables were kept. Jesus turned the most ordinary place into a place of prayer.
d3: the Lord's Prayer. It is not a magic spell to memorize and repeat, but a model showing the direction and order of prayer. The early church recited the Lord's Prayer three times a day (Didache 8).
d4: forgiveness. It means letting go of a debt you hold. Matthew describes sin as a 'debt'. The phrase 'as we also forgive our debtors' comes from this.
